description: Issue #839: when a program contains BOTH kinds of declaration-slot collision, BOTH are reported, and the one first in SOURCE ORDER is reported first. Here a duplicate `tally` on line 4 precedes a built-in `define forward` on line 7, and that is the order the findings arrive in. Issue #815 changed which stage decides this: phase-1 registration still halts at the first collision, but the check that now runs before it sees the whole program, so the later `ol-reserved-word` IS produced — what stayed worth pinning is the ORDER, because it is the order a learner reads. It remains deliberately separate from the *priority* property (`ol-reserved-word` beats `ol-duplicate-definition` when ONE name is both). The mirror program — the `define forward` block first, then the duplicated `tally` — leads with `ol-reserved-word`; it is pinned as a unit test (`execute-declaration-slots.test.mjs`, "the first collision reported is the first in source order, whichever code it carries") rather than as a second fixture, since the two differ only in block order. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy does not appear beside the check's. The other findings recorded here are independent faults in the same program, each reported once.
